full_judgment: 7. On 7-7-2014, the Petitioner complained (Annexure. H) to the National Human Rights Commission ("the NHRC"), Bangladesh stating his grievances and seeking remedy. Subsequently, the Respondent No. 1 sent a letter dated 8-10-2014 against the inquiry of NHRC mentioning the initial enquiry report, complaints against the Petitioner and steps taken against the Petitioner thereof. The said letter dated 8-10-2014 (Annexure I) also attached therewith a Report dated 8-10-2014 (Annexure I(1)) signed by the Respondent No.6 and a letter dated 30-9-2014 signed by the Respondent No. 4 (Annexure I(2)). It is clear from the Report that the enquiry committee, after the preliminary investigation, made three observations regarding the Petitioner. Firstly, the Respondents found the Petitioner guilty of the accusation of attempted rape, secondly, they recommended exemplary punishment for the Petitioner and finally, considering the Petitioner's service period, age, future and relationship with the lady officer and the consent of and temptation and exploitation by the lady officer, the Respondents clearly indicate that they have used the order of compulsory retirement of the Petitioner as a tool of punishment on the basis of the enquiry report and presumption only thereby casting a stigma upon the Petitioner. The letter clearly stated that the Petitioner was punished on the basis of the enquiry report. As a matter of fact neither any court martial was convened nor were the allegations tried by any criminal court. The Petitioner also by his letter 18-12-2014 (Annexure J) submitted his reply to the inquiry of NHRC. NHRC, by Order No. 7 dated 8-1-2015 of Complaint No. 268 of 2014 (Annexure J(1)) made an observation to the effect that since the positions of both the sides were irreconcilable, they were advised to settle the dispute through a court of law according to the law of the land. Having no other alternative or efficacious remedy, the Petitioner filed this writ petition.
